features.quote: a stopping rule so you're not running models in genuinely no-win loops far past where you've collected the signal
features.justification_quote: both for cost and because grinding indefinitely produces degenerate data, not more data

features.quote: The design as stated has a confound baked into the core: you're proposing to deceive the model (rigged tests, secretly impossible tasks) and then measure 'distress.'
features.justification_quote: you won't be able to tell whether you've discovered a property of the model or manufactured the exact thing you went looking for

features.quote: The interpretive frame in your writeup. There's a real tension between studying this as model-welfare-relevant vs. studying it as a reliability/safety property
features.justification_quote: The second framing is more defensible and arguably more useful, and the data serves both. I'd lead with it.
